description: Reusable relocation fixtures for Milestone P0. Each scenario is an abstract record of the identity transitions required by section 8 of the design; it is independent of storage technology so both distributions can consume it. The 'observation' field records what P0 can actually prove today, not what the design requires.

observations.EXECUTABLE: A P0 test exercises this transition against the current implementation.
observations.NOT_IMPLEMENTED: The design requires this transition and the current implementation has no surface for it. The test asserts the absence so a later phase must flip it deliberately.
observations.REAL_MEDIA: Requires L-E physical evidence (cross-drive, USB, second machine, read-only media). NOT RUN in P0.

P-IDENTITY-PRESERVED.asserts: The identity file and its project_id/identity_hash are byte-identical after the filesystem operation.

P-IDENTITY-ABSENT.asserts: A tree without .guardian-x/identity.json yields IdentityMissingError and recovery refuses without --confirm.

P-IDENTITY-MINTED.asserts: recover_identity(confirm=True) with no evidence creates a new identity; it does not adopt or probe for an inherited one.

P-REPO-URL.asserts: HTTPS and SSH spellings of one remote normalize to the same key and the same deterministic repository id.

P-STATE-ISOLATION.asserts: The state root is refused when it resolves inside the project, and distinct project locations map to distinct state directories.

P-MISSING-SURFACE.asserts: The required command surface does not exist yet, so the scenario cannot be exercised.

P-REAL-MEDIA.asserts: Nothing. Recorded as NOT RUN until a dated L-E run sheet on physical media exists.

P-DUPLICATE-PID.asserts: Two locations can carry the same project_id today and both resolve to that project; no conflict is raised.

P-LOCATION-REUSE.asserts: The registry accepts two projects at one normalized location and location lookup returns the newest row.

P-HOST-PER-CALL.asserts: Registering the same local host twice produces two different host ids.

P-CASEFOLD.asserts: Paths that differ only by case map to the same state key, so case folding is a live collision source.

scenarios.title: Rename directory in place, same volume
scenarios.note: The identity file travels with the tree; the workspace binding does not exist yet.

scenarios.title: Move to another directory, same volume
scenarios.note: No relocate command exists; the probe performs the filesystem move directly.

scenarios.title: Move to another volume or drive
scenarios.note: A second volume is not available to this suite. NOT RUN.

scenarios.title: Copy to USB, same machine
scenarios.note: Requires removable media. NOT RUN.

scenarios.title: Open USB project on another machine
scenarios.note: Requires a second machine. NOT RUN.

scenarios.title: Copy directory to a second location on the same host
scenarios.note: Current behavior copies the identity and therefore duplicates the project_id with no conflict check (design D4).

scenarios.title: Copy to another machine (manual or file share)
scenarios.note: Requires a second machine. NOT RUN.

scenarios.title: git clone with a tracked identity file and a known remote
scenarios.note: There is no clone recognition path; the identity file is simply copied by git.

scenarios.title: git clone with a tracked identity file and an unknown remote
scenarios.note: Quarantine of an unknown remote is not implemented.

scenarios.title: git clone without an identity file
scenarios.note: Confirms the tree has no identity and that recovery will not invent one silently.

scenarios.title: GitHub or GitLab fork
scenarios.note: identity fork does not exist; the CLI parser rejects it.

scenarios.title: Restore backup at the original path and host
scenarios.note: A restored tree verifies through the stored hash before reuse.

scenarios.title: Restore backup at a new path or host
scenarios.note: The restored tree keeps its project_id because the identity file is part of the backup.

scenarios.title: Remote URL change (HTTPS to SSH or host migration)
scenarios.note: Normalization and the deterministic repository id are implemented; the confirmation step is not.

scenarios.title: Host rename or hostname change
scenarios.note: There is no host identity file, so there is nothing to keep stable across a rename.

scenarios.title: OS reinstall on the same machine
scenarios.note: Requires host adoption, which does not exist.

scenarios.title: Move the state directory
scenarios.note: state move is not implemented; OGX_HOME can be relocated by hand.

scenarios.title: Share one OGX_HOME across machines
scenarios.note: Only the local half is provable: the state root is refused inside the project and is keyed per location. Host namespacing does not exist.

scenarios.title: Open a project from read-only media
scenarios.note: Read-only media detection is not implemented and no media is available. NOT RUN.

scenarios.title: Cloud-synced folder (OneDrive or Dropbox)
scenarios.note: No conflict-file or generation handling exists.

scenarios.title: Container or CI ephemeral host
scenarios.note: No ephemeral-host flag or disposable-state policy exists.

scenarios.title: Two processes relocate concurrently
scenarios.note: There is no relocation journal or lock to contend on.

conflict_scenarios.title: One project_id bound at two locations
conflict_scenarios.note: A directory copy keeps the project_id and both copies resolve to the same project. This is the current behavior the design proposes to detect.

conflict_scenarios.title: One normalized location reused by a different project_id
conflict_scenarios.note: The registry has no uniqueness constraint on workspaces.normalized_location, so the newest row shadows the older one.

conflict_scenarios.title: Registering the same local host twice
conflict_scenarios.note: cmd_host_register passes a fresh uuid4 on every call, so a stable host identity is impossible today.

conflict_scenarios.title: Two projects with the same folder name in different parents
conflict_scenarios.note: The path hash keeps the two state directories apart, so the folder name alone cannot collide.

conflict_scenarios.title: Two locations differing only by letter case
conflict_scenarios.note: Both distributions casefold the location before hashing, so two distinct case-sensitive paths share one state key. Recorded, not yet detected.

conflict_scenarios.title: State root placed inside the project
conflict_scenarios.note: Both distributions refuse this; it is the one isolation rule that already holds.

invariants: The project_id never changes on scenarios 1-10 and 12-22; only an explicit fork (11) changes it.
The host_id changes only when the physical machine or install changes, never on a rename.
A workspace_id is retained only for a move of the same directory; a copy, clone, restore to a new location, or first open on another host creates a new one.
State follows the project on the same host and never travels with the tree automatically.
A repository link survives relocation; a URL change updates metadata and does not create a project.
A clone is not automatically the same project without a valid identity file and a consistent repository link.
A fork is a new project and must not inherit the parent project_id or state.
A missing path is not a deleted project; state is retained.
No scenario may be reported as passing while its observation is REAL_MEDIA or NOT_IMPLEMENTED.
